answers.core:
It should be core because it more closely follows other, similar Nodes like a `RayCast3D`'s `enabled` property or a `CollisionShape3D`'s `disabled` property. Solving it through scripting means it is more brittle; in the unlikely case that more properties are added or renamed, the scripted solution could introduce subtle bugs.

It appears to me that the "*enabled" naming is a more used nomenclature in Godot than "disabled" and `CollisionShape3D`'s is an outlier but I haven't looked into it very closely. Either `enabled` or `disabled` would be fine.
answers.workaround: It could be done in script by saving and restoring the state of all of `RemoteTransform3D`'s properties in an `enabled` setter in a subclass of `RemoteTransform3D`.

title: Add `enabled` to `RemoteTransform3D` to control whether it affects the 'Remote Path'
